findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false through inverted dead logic
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions), returns false when that value is true, and also returns false when it is false. The feature flag therefore has no effect and the branching is misleading: a maintainer trying to re-enable SQL expressions by restoring the flag check can easily invert the logic and either keep the feature permanently disabled or accidentally enable the unsafe DuckDB path. The helper should directly express the intended temporary disable (return false with a clear comment) or correctly return the flag value once the stub is removed.

findings.title: Legacy SQL command entry point is not explicitly disabled
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand still accepts SQL expressions and calls NewSQLCommand without any feature-flag or disabled-feature check. It is only blocked incidentally because sql.TablesList now calls the stub DB and errors, producing a generic 'error reading SQL command' BadRequest. This leaves two different disable behaviours for SQL expressions (explicit rejection in ExpressionQueryReader versus an incidental parsing failure here), and if the stub DB's RunCommands/TablesList is ever partially restored this legacy path would again create executable SQLCommands without passing through the reader's guard. The legacy unmarshalling path should reject QueryTypeSQL explicitly as well.

findings.title: No tests cover SQL-expression rejection and existing SQL tests are not updated
findings.body: The PR disables SQL expressions in ReadQuery and stubs pkg/expr/sql.DB so TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto always return 'not implemented', but it adds no test asserting that a SQL expression is rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, and it does not update or skip the pre-existing tests that exercise TablesList/SQLCommand execution against DuckDB. Those existing tests will now fail against the stub, while the security-critical rejection path itself remains unprotected against regression. Add a reader test for the disabled SQL type and skip/remove/update the DuckDB-dependent tests accordingly.
